headline: Mayo Clinic researchers built an AI model called REDMOD that spotted signs of pancreatic cancer on earlier routine CT scans that had been read as normal.
score_reason: Pool 6 lowered by 2: the study was announced on 29 Apr 2026 and the pool page is a months-old morning roundup that the feed re-dated, so it is not today's news.
importance_line: Pancreatic cancer is usually found late, so a tool that reads faint signs on scans already taken could one day help people at higher risk, but the results come from earlier scans tested after the fact, the model also flagged some healthy people, and it still needs testing in high-risk groups.
summary: Medical Economics reports on a Mayo Clinic study in the journal Gut in which REDMOD flagged 73 percent of pancreatic cancers on routine abdominal CT scans taken a median of about 16 months before diagnosis, nearly double the rate of specialists reading the same images without the AI. This is not new today: the study was announced on 29 Apr 2026, and ScienceAlert's coverage adds that the model also wrongly flagged 81 of 430 healthy people's scans and still needs testing in larger and high-risk groups.
notes: Older news re-dated: the Medical Economics page is a roundup written in about late April 2026 (it speaks of Purdue ceasing operations 'May 1' in the future tense). Mayo Clinic's own release returned 403; the extra figures come from ScienceAlert, which was read in full. Outlets differ on scan counts, so none is printed.
